reading.body:
Tecnodati S.R.L. is an unverified OpenStreetMap point in Italy, tagged as a data center but carrying no power figure, no operator, and no website.

The record has a name that fits its tag: "dati" is Italian for data, and the S.R.L. suffix marks a real corporate form. That makes it more plausible than other Italian entries in the same dataset whose names point to accounting, foam manufacturing, or auto clubs. But plausibility is not confirmation. The research note states plainly that no operator site, press coverage, or business registration was checked, because search quota ran out.

For AI infrastructure, the entry carries no capacity signal. The power field is zero, which here means unrecorded rather than zero megawatts, and no suitability score is attached. A single mapped node at these coordinates cannot be counted as compute supply, and it cannot be counted as demand either. It is a candidate location awaiting verification.

What the data does not cover: whether any building exists at the coordinates, what it contains, whether it draws power, and whether the tag was applied correctly. The nearest airport, Parma at 18.6 miles, is the only corroborating geographic detail. Treat this as a lead, not a facility.
